newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SWIMMING-FINA TAKES CONTROL OF WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-FINA TAKES CONTROL OF WORLD CUP.

text.p: FINA, world swimming's governing body, said on Monday it had reclaimed control of the swimming World Cup.
FINA director Cornel Marculescu said it did so at the request of the national federations which had been running the competition since FINA handed it over three years ago.
An agreement under which FINA allowed the federations to give the series of short-course meetings the title of World Cup is coming to an end.
FINA told the federations it was not prepared to let the series continue to be called the World Cup unless it was involved.
"For the last two years FINA has not been involved and we have just allowed the federations to use the word `world' in the competition," Marculescu said.
"The competition has taken on much greater importance recently and the level keeps getting higher. From now on the World Cup will be run under FINA rules and its control."
